doc.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: What Charlie Parker was like to play behind
summary: Hyman did not know Parker well; the few times he played with him Parker was pleasant and workmanlike.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Most of them are somehow. Do you remember what was it like to play behind him? At that time was it like kind of, did it make you nervous to be behind someone like that? Because to us now he’s such an icon. But what was his reputation at that time?

He was very pleasant. I mean I didn’t know Charlie Parker really, I didn’t hang out with him. I didn’t participate in any of the legendary all night sessions. I certainly didn’t get high with him. But when I, the couple of times I played with him, and there is also one set at Birdland as I remember when Bud Powell didn’t show up, he was just very pleasant and workmanlike, and quite agreeable.
